record.paper_title: Monetary Stabilization in Cryptocurrencies—Design Approaches and Open Questions
record.context_brief: Margin calls in illiquid collateral markets
record.original_question: Can margin-call mechanisms for proxy-collateralized or self-collateralized stablecoins remain robust when collateral markets are small, young, or illiquid, or when expectations about the collateral’s future value deteriorate?

evidence.quote:
Margin calls
are often cited as a remedy for collateral risk, however, margin
calls require the assumption that markets for the collateral
asset are liquid and large enough to allow for timely provision
or absorption of collateral. This assumption might become an
issue for young stablecoin projects or if expectations on the
future development of the collateral are dire.

On the other hand, proxy and self
collateralization (promising alternative techniques that might
be applicable in “trustless” settings) rely heavily on margin
calls with questionable robustness. Further research is required
to evaluate the viability of such margin calls in small and po-
tentially illiquid markets.

artifact.status_search_result: The robustness of margin-call mechanisms for proxy- and self-collateralized stablecoins in small or illiquid markets remains an active research area. Subsequent work on crypto-collateralized stablecoins (e.g., analyses of MakerDAO's Black Thursday March 2020 event, deleveraging spirals, and stablecoin attack literature) documents instability under stressed liquidity but does not provide a definitive positive resolution. No general result establishing robustness has been published; the question is widely treated as open.

status_evidence.title: Stablecoins 2.0: Economic Foundations and Risk-based Models
status_evidence.snippet: Studies deleveraging spirals and instability of crypto-collateralized stablecoins under illiquid conditions, indicating margin-call robustness is not guaranteed.
status_evidence.claim: The robustness of margin calls for crypto-collateralized stablecoins in illiquid markets remains an open and active question.

status_evidence.title: An Analysis of the Market Risk to Participants in the Compound Protocol
status_evidence.snippet: Analyzes liquidation mechanisms in DeFi and shows that thin liquidity and adverse price impact can cause cascading liquidations.
status_evidence.claim: Empirical and modeling work shows margin-call mechanisms can fail under thin liquidity, supporting that the original question is unresolved.
